thread:
ashley: Heads-up — saw a spike in requests still routing to v1 last night during the US evening window. Console shows a handful of tenants with sticky-route TTLs > 24h. Not sure if it's telemetry mislabeling or actual affinity leak. Anyone else?
raj: saw that too. telemetry shows sticky_count bump at 03:12 UTC then gradual decay but some tenants stayed steady.
marta: could be the client lib fallback when it hits 429 from v2 and retries without the version header. we added an implicit-handshake in the SDK months ago.
sam: can you paste the sample headers we saw?
ashley: sure — example from logs: 
```
X-Redwood-Client-Version: 1.0.1
X-Redwood-Route-Affinity: v2
X-Redwood-Route-TTL: 86400
```
But payloads processed by proxy had no header and still got sticky routing applied.
raj: interesting — proxy code gives priority to existing affinity cookie before incoming header. if the cookie is long-lived and the client drops header on retry, proxy keeps the cookie.
marta: this matches a pattern where clients retry without headers on network failure. fallback path is v1 which sets cookie TTL long. so an accidental long TTL on v1 is the root.
ashley: proposal: for the next canary, set v1 default affinity TTL to 15m for new cookies and add a console hint that tenants with >6h TTL show potential fallback leakage.
lisa: UI/console note: we can add a badge "suspect fallback" under route health. Do we want to surface counts or an estimated token cost?
sam: counts + estimated extra spend would be helpful. Cost calc: extra_tokens * price_rate. low fidelity is fine.
raj: also want a safer server-side mitigation: if we see >3 rapid toggles v1<->v2 for a token id within 5m, force a stateless routing for next request (no cookie) and log. reduces oscillation.
marta: agree but need to be cautious — some workloads rely on affinity for KV cache hit. stateless kill could hurt latency. maybe only apply to tenants above threshold (e.g., <50ms p95 impact if stateless)
ashley: good call. let's make it tenant-gated. run a 1% tenant shadow experiment first.
deploy-bot: canary rollout queued: affinity-ttl-reduce-v1 -> 1% -> Mon 09:00 UTC
sam: roadmap: 1) telemetry QA to identify affected tenants 2) console badge + cost estimate 3) server-side oscillation breaker 4) SDK doc update to keep headers on retries
lisa: I'll draft console copy. short and actionable: "Your traffic shows repeated fallback to legacy API — consider updating SDK or toggling affinity settings."
raj: one more telemetry ask: we need a signal that correlates client-lib-version + missing header + sequence of 429s. that'll help confirm client behavior.
marta: I can add a sampling probe to pipeline that annotates traces with client headers; low overhead.
ashley: thanks. timeline? try to have telemetry and TTL change in the canary within 48h. console badge in next sprint.
sam: ack. tagging @marta for instrumentation task, @lisa for UI draft, @raj for server breaker PR.
marta: will start on probe today.
lisa: will send copy by EOD.
raj: will sketch breaker implementation and perf test.
ashley: great. If we see regression, we rollback affinity TTL change first. :thumbsup:
sam: noted. also add a dashboard card under "Routing -> Fallbacks" highlighting oscillation rate.
ashley: perfect. thanks everyone.
